scope: Proposition 9.2 (Quenched transfer of a finite strip family) of the manuscript “Quenched SLE₃ Universality for the Weak Random-Bond Ising Model” (preprints/Quenched-SLE3-Universality-for-the-Weak-Random-Bond-Ising-Model-October-5-2026/quenched-sle3-weak-random-bond-ising.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dbf1578546653fc5), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 51. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix h > 0 and a finite family of allowed plus strips in A− h . Let Σ− h,n have the pure Dobrushin spin law in an ordinary lattice approximation of A− h , and let Σn,ω have the target spin law. These samples admit couplings conditional on ω whose two marginals are the stated laws and for which P  every strip crossed by plus in Σ− h,n is crossed by plus in Σn,ω  = 1 − o(1). (9.2) The probability in (9.2) includes environment and coupling randomness. The pure marginal conditional on ω is its deterministic Dobrushin law. The corresponding assertion holds for minus strips in A+ h .
